accuracyChecks.method: Two rounds of 5 random items per chapter (13 chapters; round 2 limited to numerical/case/long items) plus 5 mock items, re-solved by hand (means, medians, modes, r, rs, index numbers, PPF/MOC, utility, budget line, elasticity, costs, profit, equilibrium, ceilings/floors); every generator also run once and its output re-solved before the build
fixes: missing-frequency generator could produce unsorted/duplicate X values (common step now fixed per item)
market demand/supply schedules had unsorted prices; now ascending
profit-maximisation MCQ had a distractor (q-1 units) with equal profit; removed and the key notes the tie
household budget case could offer two items that were jointly affordable; items now always exceed the remaining income together
non-sampling-error family could never build (only one sampling-error row); replaced by a NOT-type item; classification table extended so odd-one-out works
break-even tables now have an interior minimum AC; Pearson data no longer produce negative Y values

mock 6-mark slots now draw only true 6-mark families (custom kind long6) instead of any C4 written item; added computed 6-mark items (PPF, elasticity, cost table, profit maximisation, equilibrium with price ceiling, mean-median-mode)
wording: "1p"/"1x" coefficients tidied, gender-neutral project stems, "headings ... are called", table-presentation key made mark-neutral, students/workers named in mean and median stems
accuracyChecks.note: Facts follow NCERT Statistics for Economics and Introductory Microeconomics; no textbook passage is reproduced. All numerical answers are computed in code.
